# Exploratory analysis

Goals - Identify the best threshold to remove noise; improve quantitative predictions from ML - plotting distributions

## Preliminary setup

```{r loadStuff}
library(tidyverse, quietly = TRUE)
library(magrittr) # for special Tee pipe operator %T>% (Error check, unique WT before calc)
library(patchwork) # for combining plots

# import functions
source("functions/0.data_processing.R")
source("functions/1.plotting.R")
source("functions/2.contribution_table.R")

# locate the data
base_path <- "enrichment_data/theoAptzepPCR_lokya/"
# file_path <- str_c(base_path, "subset.tsv") # for testing
file_path <- str_c(base_path, "DiMSum_Project_variant_data_merge.tsv") # for production

# global variables
expected_variants <- 135000 # (epPCR) from colony counts (source: Lokya)
count_tracker <- tibble(
  threshold = numeric(),
  variants = numeric(),
  input_reads = numeric(),
  filtered_columns = character()) # global variable to track counts at different thresholds
```

## Data cleanup

- Select relevant columns
- Clean up column names
- Calculate enrichment, leak metrics Ref: \_Borrowing some code from DiMSum/[split-multiinputs.R](https://github.com/ppreshant/DiMSum/blob/master/scripts/split_multiinputs.R)

```{r data-cleanup}
data <- read_and_cleanup_data(file_path)
cat("Column names: ", paste(colnames(data), collapse = ", "), "\n")

total_variants <- nrow(data)
total_reads <- sum(data$Input_count)
count_tracker <- count_tracker |> 
  add_row(threshold = 0,
          variants = total_variants, input_reads = total_reads,
          filtered_columns = "")

cat("Total variants: ", format(total_variants, big.mark = ","), "\n")
cat("Total reads: ", format(total_reads, big.mark = ","), "\n")
```

## Raw visualization

```{r raw_count_distribution}
#| fig-width: 2
#| fig-height: 3

# nham_variant_count_distribution(head(data, 1000)) # top 1,000 data
var_raw <- nham_variant_count_distribution(data) # all data
read_raw <- nham_read_count_distribution(data)
```

Plotting the distribution of reads in the raw data, selection counts, and leak counts. This will help us understand the distribution of reads across different categories.

```{r raw_read_distribution}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 4

patch_read_dist_multi_columns(data) + 
  plot_annotation(title = "Distribution of reads in raw data",
                  subtitle = "Comparing input, selection and leak counts. Note log10 scale on y-axis")

```

Looking at the distribution of reads, we can see that there are a lot of variants with low counts. We want to filter out these low-count variants to reduce noise in our analysis.

# Filtering within Input, Selection, and Leak counts

Table of variant counts and input reads at different thresholds


```{r filter_set1_allthresholds}
thresholds <- c(1, 2, 5, 10, 100)

filter_list_25 <- 
  map(thresholds, 
    filter_data, df = data, filter_columns = c("Input_count", "Selection_count", "Leak_count"))

count_log_25 <- bind_rows(count_tracker, 
  map(filter_list_25, \(x) x$count_tracker) |> 
  bind_rows())

```

## Variant counts vs expected

```{r variant_counts_vs_expected}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 2

# plot the variant counts vs expected variants from count_tracker

ggplot(count_tracker, aes(x = threshold, y = variants)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_point() +

  # expected variants line
  geom_hline(yintercept = expected_variants, linetype = "dashed") +
  annotate("text", 
    x = max(count_tracker$threshold) * 0.7, 
    y = expected_variants + max(count_tracker$variants)/10, 
    label = str_c("Expected: ", format(expected_variants, big.mark = ","), " variants")) +

  labs(title = "Variant Counts with thresholds",
       x = "Count Threshold",
       y = "Number of Variants") +
  theme_minimal()

```

# Indel analysis

## Read count distribution

```{r indel_read_distribution}
#| fig-width: 2
#| fig-height: 3

WT_len <- data |>
  filter(Nham_nt == 0) |>
  pull(sequence_length) |>
  unique() # get WT length 

indels <- data |>
  filter(is.na(Nham_nt)) |> # filter for indels
  mutate(indel_length = sequence_length - WT_len) # calculate indel length

read_distribution(indels)
```

## Variant distribution by sequence length

```{r indel_distribution_by_length}
#| fig-width: 4
#| fig-height: 5

# indel_variant_counts <- summarise(indels, count = n(), .by = indel_length) # summarize to get variant counts at each Nham_nt value

indel_variant_dist <- 
  ggplot(indels, aes(y = indel_length)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", colour = "black") + 
  # geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  # annotate("text", 
  #   x = 0.9 * max(indel_variant_counts$count),
  #   y = 0, 
  #   label = "WT length", 
  #   hjust = 1, vjust = -1) +
  labs(title = "Indel Variant Distribution by Sequence Length",
       x = "Number of Variants",
       y = "Indel Length (nt)") +
  theme_minimal()

# indel read distr
indel_read_counts <- summarise(indels, count = sum(Input_count), .by = indel_length) # summarize to get variant counts at each Nham_nt value

indel_read_dist <- 
  ggplot(indel_read_counts, aes(x = count, y = indel_length)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, color = "steelblue") +
  # xlim(0, 5000)
  scale_x_log10() +
  # geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "steelblue") + 
  labs(title = "Indel Read Distribution by Sequence Length",
       x = "Number of Reads",
       y = "Indel Length (nt)") +
  theme_minimal()

# combine the two plots
indel_variant_dist + indel_read_dist + plot_layout(axes = "collect") + 
  plot_annotation(title = "Indel Variant and Read Distribution by Sequence Length",
                  subtitle = "Comparing number of variants and number of reads for each indel length. Note log10 scale on x-axis for read distribution")
```

# Catalysis/leak analysis 

## Distributions

### >= 1 count
```{r catalysis_leak_distribution}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 4


cat_dist <- read_distribution(d1, "relative_catalysis")
leak_dist <- read_distribution(d1, "relative_leak")
net_cat_dist <- read_distribution(d1, "net_catalysis")

(cat_dist + leak_dist + net_cat_dist +
  plot_layout(ncol = 3)+
  plot_annotation(title = "Distribution of catalysis and leak scores; >= 1 count",
    subtitle = "Comparing catalysis, leak and net catalysis scores. Note log10 scale on y-axis") 
) & 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, color = "red") 
```

## Comparing catalysis and leak scores 

### >= 1

```{r}
perc_cat_leak <- d1 |>
  summarise(frac_cat_leak = 100 * sum(relative_catalysis > relative_leak, na.rm = TRUE) / nrow(d1)) |>
  pull(frac_cat_leak)

```

`{r} perc_cat_leak`% of variants have higher catalysis scores than leak scores in the filtered data (count >= 1).

```{r catalysis_leak_comparison1}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 3

ggplot(d1, aes(y = relative_catalysis, x = relative_leak)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1, colour = "black") +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Comparison of Catalysis and Leak Scores",
        y = "Catalysis, WT normalized",
        x = "Leak, WT normalized") +
  theme_minimal()

```

### >= 10


```{r catalysis_leak_comparison10}
#| fig-width: 5
#| fig-height: 3

ggplot(d10, aes(y = relative_catalysis, x = relative_leak)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.1, colour = "black") +
  scale_x_log10() + scale_y_log10() +

  labs(title = "Comparison of Catalysis and Leak Scores",
        y = "Catalysis, WT normalized",
        x = "Leak, WT normalized") +

```


## outliners? 

What are these outliers at the edges (-Inf / zeros before log10 transformation)? Let's check how many variants have zero catalysis or leak scores.
```{r calcs}
#| echo: false

zero_cat_d1 <- filter(d1, relative_catalysis == 0) |> nrow()
zero_leak_d1 <- filter(d1, relative_leak == 0) |> nrow()

d1cat0 <- filter(d1, relative_catalysis == 0)
```

`{r} zero_cat_d1` variants have zero catalysis scores and `{r} zero_leak_d1` variants have zero leak scores in the filtered data (count >= 1).

## Net catalysis scores across the ribozyme sequence

The table below counts substitutions and sums the WT-normalised score changes
for each destination nucleotide at each position. Indels are excluded, and a multi-mutant contributes its complete score change to each of its substitutions.

```{r contribution_d1_net_cat}
contribution1 <- make_contribution_table(d1)

# contribution1 |> filter(total_mutations > 0) |> 
#   View(title = "contr1")

# plot total_net catalysis across positions
contribution1 |> 
  # filter(total_mutations > 0) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = position, y = total_net_catalysis_mean)) +
  geom_point() + geom_line(alpha = 0.4) +

  # annotations for positions of interest
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, color = "red") + 
  annotate("rect", xmin = 21, xmax = 27, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.1, fill = "orange") + # ribozyme core

  # communication modules
  annotate("rect", xmin = 49, xmax = 53, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.1, fill = "blue") +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 73, xmax = 77, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.1, fill = "blue") +
  # geom_annotate("rect", xmin = 73, xmax = 77, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.1, fill = "grey") +

  labs(title = "Distribution of total net catalysis mean across positions") +
  theme_minimal()

```
